C0.quote: Justified Representation (JR)/Extended Justified Representation (EJR) is a desirable axiom in multiwinner approval voting.
C0.note: Multiwinner approval voting rules; committee selection.

C1.quote: we show that it is NP-hard to approximate MDJR and MDEJR
C1.note: Main results are approximation, hardness and FPT; a new axiomatic-style property (degree) is proposed, but the results are algorithmic.

C2.3.note: The paper also speaks of 'a profile A of n approval preferences', but no separate held attitude is defined. Mentions of preferences and satisfaction are loose.

C2.4.quote: Given a profile A of 𝑛 approval preferences
C2.4.note: Approval ballots are also called approval preferences, and the rule is applied directly with no statement about submission or sincerity.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.quote: each voter’s “utility” is defined by the harmonic progression
C4.1.note: The format is approval, and voter satisfaction and utility are used. The PAV utility is defined directly from the number of approved winners, and satisfaction is the number of approved winners. Applicability is borderline. The link is effectively specified, but I code SPEC.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' appears only in a reference title.

C5.1.quote: at least 𝑐 voters in every cohesive group are represented
C5.1.note: The (E)JR degree measures representation of voters.

C5.2.quote: there are at least 𝑐 voters each of which approves at least 1 candidate
C5.2.note: Evaluated on approval ballots, with no statement relating them to held attitudes.
